hint: A base ten log asks which power of $10$ gives the number inside. What power gives $1000$?

hints.text: A base ten log asks which power of $10$ gives the number inside. What power gives $1000$?
Write $1000$ as $10 \times 10 \times 10$ and count how many tens were multiplied together.
Three tens are used, so $10^3 = 1000$ and $\log_{10}(1000) = 3$.

explanation: A base $10$ log asks how many tens are multiplied together to make the number.
Three tens make a thousand, which is written $10^3 = 1000$.
The exponent is the value of the log, so $\log_{10}(1000) = 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the zeros
steps: With base $10$, the answer is simply the number of zeros.
So $\log_{10}(1000) = 3$. Check: $100$ has two zeros and $\log_{10}(100) = 2$.
